title: Canvas tool taxonomy - Mask / Paint / Composite groups and a floating Detect strip
description:
Agreed with the user in the MPI-424 brainstorm 2026-08-01. This lands FIRST: it is the frame every other canvas card mounts into, and building Adjust, Shapes, Paint or Composite before it means building each of them twice.

THE PROBLEM: the Mask group in the left toolbar (MpiHistoryTools IMAGE_TOOLS) is four buttons today - brush, points, text, detect - and three of those four are the same job with a different engine. Shapes and Adjust would make it six. Paint and Composite would add four more. The toolbar column grows without bound and the user cannot tell which buttons produce the same artifact.

THE STRUCTURE (user's own, not derived):
  Mask       [brush] [detect ->] [adjust] [shapes]
  Paint      [brush] [shapes]
  Composite  [mask comp] [paint comp]
Detect is a COLLAPSE BUTTON: clicking it opens a small vertical strip OUTSIDE the tool panel, next to the toolbar, holding points / text / auto (the old Detect). It dismisses itself on a timer while unhovered so it cannot sit there forever. No corner triangle, no long-press - the user rejected both explicitly.

WHAT THIS IS NOT: the three detect modes are NOT collapsed into one mode. They stay maskPoints / maskText / maskDetect in TOOL_OPTIONS_REGISTRY and in _MASK_TOOLS; only their PRESENTATION changes, from three stacked toolbar buttons to three entries in a floating strip. That keeps this card to tool-list defs plus one new component. An earlier draft of this design collapsed the modes themselves and was dropped as unnecessary work.

TWO ENGINES, SIX BUTTONS: Mask Brush and Paint Brush are ONE brush engine with two destinations (binary mask layers vs the RGBA paint layer); Mask Shapes and Paint Shapes are ONE shape gizmo with the same split. This card only declares the modes and the groups - the engines are extracted by MPI-375 (brush) and MPI-368 (gizmo), each of which now ships two mounts instead of one tool.

REVERSES A RECORDED DECISION: MpiHistoryTools.js carries the comment 'Shapes (MPI-368) joins this group; it does not become a switcher'. That was written when the family was four hand-picked methods. Update the comment with the new reasoning rather than leaving it contradicting the code.
acceptance: IMAGE_TOOLS in MpiHistoryTools reads: Mask (brush, detect, adjust, shapes), Paint (brush, shapes), Composite (mask comp, paint comp) - the new modes may be declared before their panels exist only if they are disabled with a reason, never dead
Clicking Detect opens a floating vertical strip outside the tool panel holding points / text / auto; picking one activates that mode exactly as the old toolbar button did
The floating strip dismisses itself on an unhovered timer, and on Escape and on any tool activation - it can never be left orphaned on screen
The strip obeys the teardown contract: every Events.on / window listener / observer / timer it creates is cleaned in destroy(), collected in a _unsubs array (see .claude/rules/components.md)
The three detect modes stay separate modes in TOOL_OPTIONS_REGISTRY and _MASK_TOOLS - presentation changes, plumbing does not

The PromptBox gate is decided and recorded for each NEW group: mask tools keep the box (MPI-372, a mask and a prompt are one operation); decide deliberately whether paint and composite modes do, and write the answer into _modeKeepsPromptBox rather than letting it fall out of _isMaskTool by accident
tests/mask-tool-registry.test.cjs is extended so a tool present in one list and missing from the other fails a test - negative-controlled in both directions, as the MPI-381 guard was
The MpiHistoryTools comment about Shapes not becoming a switcher is updated to the new reasoning, not left contradicting the code
docs/masking.md records the taxonomy - artifact per group, method per button, engine shared across groups - within its 200-line cap (trim first)
